title: Let the Kids Play

description.main: Pax Paloscia's Let the Kids Play, part of Drago's 36 Chambers series, mixes street photographs of children and teenagers with drawings, graffiti and paintings. The Roman artist treats childhood as a stance against the cynicism of adult life rather than an age. Published in Rome in 2007 as a 96-page softcover.
description.extended:
Let the Kids Play gathers the Roman artist Pax Paloscia's photographs, drawings and paintings of children and teenagers, and treats childhood as a stance against the adult world rather than an age.

Drago published it in Rome in 2007 in its 36 Chambers series, a 96-page softcover, 17 by 24 cm, printed in black and white. Street photographs of kids made in different cities sit beside stencil-like illustrations, graffiti and painted pages. It opens on a line from Carl Jung, "The creative mind plays with the objects it loves." The writer Laura Lombardi introduces it as an intimate diary, like the box of useless treasures a child keeps hidden. The title names a condition, not an age group. It refuses the cynicism and routine of adult life through the symbolic objects of a child's world.

Paloscia (b. Rome, 1974) trained at the Academy of Illustration and Image in Rome and worked in Milan from the age of 22 as a freelance illustrator. She graduated from the International Center of Photography in New York in 2007. Street culture and the world of children run through her photography, painting, drawing and video. She divides her time between New York and Rome, and showed recent pictures of Staten Island kids at MIA Photo Fair in Milan in 2026.
description.artist_bio: Pax Paloscia (b. Rome, 1974) studied at the Academy of Illustration and Image, Rome; freelance illustrator in Milan from age 22 (Rolling Stone, Feltrinelli, Mondadori, Nike, Levi's and others); graduated from ICP New York in 2007. Works across photography, painting, drawing and video, influenced by street culture and the world of kids; based between New York and Rome. Group show Ciao Maschio, Galleria Comunale d'Arte Moderna, Rome, 2021; shown at MIA Photo Fair BNP Paribas, Milan, 2026 (Staten Island kids series, RAW Messina).

notes: Shelf: Mixed. Drago 36 Chambers series (listed by dealers as volume 8; not stated on the Drago page). Text by Laura Lombardi; Carl Jung epigraph. Drago gives 17 x 24 cm; ACC Art Books lists 14 x 17 cm (5.51 x 6.69 in) and 89 b&w illustrations; publisher's figure used. Amazon UK lists a 2010 Drago International Entertainment printing of the same ISBN.
